authority_context.task_title: Materialize the proof-slice design package for Component Design Planning Service

source_statements: Component Design Planning Service is the first Stratum 2 domain service with enough upstream maturity to act as the proof slice for the refined PAA derivation process.

The dry run proved that PAA can derive a strong draft brief body for this service, but cannot yet produce fully governed execution authority without a real slice package, service-oriented target taxonomy, and explicit brief lifecycle governance.
The producer-side derivation subsystem must move from reviewed System Design to DesignPackage, CoderBrief, BriefTarget, and packet-ready authority without manual architectural invention.
product_and_source_basis.product_outcome_statement: Materialize a real Stage 1 authority package for Component Design Planning Service so the refined PAA derivation path can be proven against a service-oriented slice instead of a documentation-only dry run.
protected_product_truths: The preferred layered architecture remains the semantic backbone for the proof slice.
Component Design Planning Service remains a narrow Domain Service and does not absorb brief assembly, workflow, or runtime orchestration responsibilities.
Repository access stays behind ComponentDesignRepository and no direct SQL or host-surface behavior is introduced into the service slice.
roadmap_context: This remediation run is the first item in Priority 0 of the derivation remediation backlog.
The slice package must exist before the service-oriented target taxonomy and execution-authority lifecycle can be proven cleanly.
This package is the upstream authority artifact for the next multi-run derivation remediation sequence.

requirements: The proof slice must be represented by one task-bound Stage 1 DesignPackage with explicit authority context, slice scope, component assignment, dependency shape, and verification basis.
The package must authorize only the Component Design Planning Service implementation slice and keep adjacent service, workflow, and producer orchestration work out of scope.
The package must be concrete enough that later coder-brief derivation can proceed without reconstructing the slice from prose notes alone.
requirement_sources: Component Design Planning Service component spec

design_decisions: Treat this package as a real Stage 1 authority artifact rather than another dry-run note.
Bind the slice to a PAA-internal task identity even though no external GitHub issue exists for this proof run.
Approve the package for derivation while explicitly carrying the remaining service-target-taxonomy and brief-lifecycle blockers as downstream remediation, not hidden assumptions.
decision_requirements: normalize the proof slice into the real derivation pipeline
keep the proof slice narrowly service-oriented
surface downstream blockers without hiding them in informal thread context
decision_rationale: The main failure in Phase 6 was not missing service design quality; it was the lack of a normalized, task-bound DesignPackage and execution-authority lifecycle around the slice.
Binding the slice to explicit task identity lets the PAA system teach the derivation process to coder agents using the same structures it expects other projects to use.

spec_fragment.spec_fragment_title: Component Design Planning Service initial implementation slice
spec_fragment.canonical_statement: Implement Component Design Planning Service as a narrow Domain Service that interprets structured component-design records into planning-friendly outputs for brief derivation and producer-side authoring, without absorbing workflow, orchestration, or persistence ownership.

current_gap: The service has a reviewed component spec but no materialized Stage 1 package and no authoritative task binding.
The current code-artifact target taxonomy is repository-shaped and does not yet encode service-oriented artifact targets needed for this slice.
The current derivation lifecycle does not yet govern the transition from draft brief to approved brief to packet-ready execution authority cleanly.
desired_state: The proof slice is represented by a real DesignPackage bound to a concrete PAA task.
The slice can later derive a governed coder brief using explicit service-oriented code-artifact targets.
The resulting implementation run remains narrowly scoped to the Component Design Planning Service package and dedicated tests.
protected_baseline: No implementation code is written during this package-materialization run.
The existing layered architecture, producer derivation subsystem model, and component spec remain the authority basis for the slice.
No workflow, runtime-event, or repository-schema ownership is redefined by this slice package.
pre_handoff_scope_checks: The service-oriented code-artifact target taxonomy has been extended before execution-authoritative derivation resumes.
The draft -> approved -> packet-ready lifecycle is explicit enough to govern this slice cleanly.
No repository SQL, workflow semantics, or host-surface wiring is pulled into the service slice.
out_of_scope_items: schema migration work beyond derivation-governance support

required_architecture_seams: Keep Component Design Planning Service in the Domain Services layer.
Keep component-design persistence access behind ComponentDesignRepository.
Keep target sequencing, producer orchestration, and packet preparation outside this service.
target_module_boundaries: The service may assemble planning DTOs but may not own packet assembly or workflow-state decisions.
architectural_authority_constraints.max_responsibility_expansion: This slice may implement only the Component Design Planning Service package and its dedicated tests; it may not grow into adjacent producer-side orchestration or runtime-lifecycle work.
forbidden_module_growth_patterns: Do not turn the service into a producer-side orchestration blob.
Do not introduce raw SQL or direct DB process management into the service package.
Do not silently extend the code-artifact taxonomy from inside service implementation code.
forbidden_dependency_shortcuts: Do not bypass ComponentDesignRepository with direct database calls.
Do not depend on GitHub issue state, runtime queue state, or installed execution-package file reads.
Do not import workflow-lifecycle or execution-package-resolution services into this slice.
architectural_anti_goals: Avoid recreating a mixed-responsibility god service.
Avoid letting derivation-governance gaps force architectural invention inside the implementation slice.

component_roles: interpret stable component-design records into planning-ready structures
consume planning outputs during brief derivation
coordinate derivation flow around planning outputs

surface_responsibilities: service package defines the interface, planning DTOs, and default implementation
dedicated unit tests prove service behavior without piggybacking on repository tests
the component spec remains the reviewed authority source for service boundaries and invariants

nodes.component_role: interpret structured component design into planning-ready outputs
capture service-level diagnostic output without changing service ownership

edges.notes: The service consumes repository interfaces and the first read/write slice is already implemented.
Logging is required by the component spec but should remain a thin injected collaborator.

sequencing_constraints.statement: Service-oriented code-artifact target taxonomy must be extended before the slice may progress from draft brief to approved execution authority.
Draft, approved, and packet-ready states must be explicitly governed before this slice is treated as execution-ready authority.

verification_obligations: The service resolves one component by stable identity and produces structured planning outputs.
The service surfaces planning gaps explicitly instead of inventing missing realization targets.
The service remains stateless and does not mutate component-design persistence by default.
Dedicated unit tests prove service behavior independently of repository SQL tests.
pass_criteria: A service-level test module can exercise the planning flows using repository doubles or fakes.
No raw SQL is introduced in the service package.
No producer or consumer host entrypoints are changed in the implementation slice.
protected_baseline_checks: Existing ComponentDesignRepository tests continue to pass.
The service package remains the only code surface changed by the future implementation run.
The component spec remains consistent with the implemented service boundary.

known_failure_modes: The service grows into producer-side orchestration instead of staying a narrow domain service.
Repository or taxonomy gaps cause the implementation to invent target shapes outside controlled vocabulary.
The slice is treated as execution-authoritative before lifecycle governance is explicit.
contamination_risks: Raw SQL or host wiring leaks into the service package.
Workflow or packet-preparation concerns are smuggled into service methods.
Taxonomy expansion is performed ad hoc inside implementation code instead of through authority updates.
recovery_hints: Fail closed when required component-design structures are missing and emit planning gaps instead of guessing.
Return the slice to draft authority if approved targets or lifecycle governance are still unresolved.
Use the package, spec, and remediation backlog as the authority basis for re-derivation rather than reconstructing scope from memory.
loop_stop_conditions: Stop if the implementation requires out-of-scope producer orchestration or workflow semantics.
Stop if the target taxonomy still cannot express the required service-oriented artifact set.
Stop if the future brief cannot progress from draft to approved to packet-ready without manual thread memory.
